etymologies.etymologyHTML: abound (third-person singular simple present abounds, present participle abounding, simple past and past participle abounded)

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To be full to overflowing; to bristle. [First attested from around (1350 to 1470).][1]
(intransitive, obsolete) To be wealthy. [Attested from around (1350 to 1470) until the mid 18th century.][1]
(intransitive) To be present or available in large numbers or quantities; to be plentiful. [First attested from around (1350 to 1470).][1]

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Romans 5:20:
quote.text: Moreouer, the Lawe entred, that the offence might abound: but where sinne abounded, grace did much more abound.

quote.citation: 1960 December, “New G.E. Line diesel loco maintenance depot at Stratford”, in Trains Illustrated, page 766:
quote.text: One end of the east-west building is wet, the other windy, and at present there is smoke abounding, too; but these distressing yard elements can be completely excluded at each end by full-width folding doors [...].

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To revel in. [Attested from around (1350 to 1470) until the late 18th century.][1]
To be copiously supplied. [with in or with ‘something’]

quote.citation: 1726 October 28, [Jonathan Swift], “A Further Account of Glubbdubdrib. […]”, in Travels into Several Remote Nations of the World.  […]  [Gulliver’s Travels], volume II, London:  […]  Benj[amin] Motte, […], →OCLC, part III (A Voyage to Laputa, Balnibarbi, Glubbdubdribb, Luggnagg, and Japan), page 108:
quote.text: I could plainly diſcover from whence one Family derives a long Chin; why a ſecond hath abounded with Knaves for two Generations, and Fools for two more; why a third happened to be crack-brained, and a fourth to be Sharpers.

quote.citation: 1858-1860, George Rawlinson, The Five Great Monarchies of the Ancient Eastern World
quote.text: the wild boar, which abounds both in Azerbijan and in the country about Hamadan
